briefing.opening: Good day. We begin today's Climate Change Daily Briefing for November 19, 2026.

sections.title: 🌍 COP31 Summit Faces Tough Negotiations as 'Fossil Fuel' References Excluded
sections.content: At the 31st UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) underway in Antalya, Türkiye, language regarding the reduction and phase-out of 'fossil fuels'—identified as the primary driver of the climate crisis—was excluded from the revised draft agreement and replaced with 'electrification' and enhanced adaptation finance targets [2, 11, 113, 118, 131]. Following climate action obstruction by fossil fuel lobbyists and the withdrawal of phase-out initiatives, climate-vulnerable nations, including Vanuatu, strongly warned against backsliding in global climate action and called for reforms to the UN climate summit process [126, 130, 136, 140]. Meanwhile, Nepal's call to streamline climate fund procedures following catastrophic flooding, compounded by financial inequalities and intensifying El Niño impacts, has brought the overall talks to a severe impasse [8, 120, 122].

sections.title: ⚠️ Accelerating Climate Damages and Stern Warnings from the Scientific Community
sections.content: Climate scientists, including Director Johan Rockström of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, have warned that delays in publishing IPCC scientific reports and attempts to block funding pose a grave threat to global climate crisis responses [96, 124, 141]. In reality, rising sea levels and increased flooding are reshaping U.S. coastlines, while in Southeast Asia, wildfires driven by El Niño and climate change are compounding public health damages across neighboring countries [101, 103]. Furthermore, invaluable human heritage, such as ancient cave paintings in Indonesia, is deteriorating at an accelerating pace due to climate change, underscoring the urgent need for a global response to the escalating human costs and psychological trauma [15, 104, 132, 135].

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic Municipalities Advance Carbon Neutrality Through Civic Engagement and Innovative Technologies
sections.content: In South Korea, tangible carbon reduction achievements by local governments and public sectors were highlighted through the '2026 Carbon Neutrality Contest' and lifestyle action evaluations [23, 41, 58]. The city of Gwangmyeong received the top award in the local government category, driven by its 'Climate Righteous Army' civic campaign that grew from 150 participants to over 20,000, while Seo-gu District in Daejeon received the Presidential Commendation for recovering 53.7 million PET bottles through an AI-powered resource circulation project [40, 46, 59]. Additionally, Geoje City won the grand prize for the second consecutive year as an outstanding municipality under the Carbon Neutrality Points program, and Chungcheongnam-do promoted its 'Chungnam-style Carbon Neutrality' policy model to the world, further strengthening international cooperation [16, 35, 50, 67].

sections.title: 🌱 Industrial Decarbonization Partnerships and Renewable Energy Infrastructure Expansion Gather Pace
sections.content: In the energy transition sector, South Korea and Australia have partnered to establish an industrial decarbonization cooperation framework to accelerate the achievement of carbon neutrality [10]. The government and relevant authorities are mandating the installation of renewable energy facilities on the roofs of newly built and expanded factories and reforming long-term contracts for the solar competitive bidding system, while hastening the development of a large-scale renewable energy market to meet surging demand driven by artificial intelligence (AI) [72, 73, 74, 85]. At the regional level, on-the-ground clean energy foundations are also being solidified, with Gochang-gun securing 1 billion KRW in national funding after being selected for a new and renewable energy convergence project, and innovative thermal energy storage companies utilizing sand and rock moving into clean tech clusters [76, 86, 89].

briefing.closing: While global climate negotiations are experiencing growing pains amid sharp conflicts of interest, practical transitions across local communities and industrial frontlines continue unabated. That concludes today's climate briefing. Thank you.
